description: Conversations, not questions. Every one of these tests a constraint that is stated once and must survive turns that do not restate it -- the thing single-turn evaluation structurally cannot see, because each of its questions carries everything it needs.
revision_note: v1.3, frozen. The first two runs of this set were a pilot -- run to expose defects in the questions and the scoring, not to read a score off, which is what the first run of any new eval set is actually for. Three problems surfaced, all in the instrument: (1) the trend turn demanded the literal "79%" while the agent writes "79.0%"; (2) an answer that led with FY2024 and added neighbouring years as context was scored as fabricating three percentages that were real, cited and from the same tool result -- so allowed_pct_values now lists every real figure, which is what it is for, and the burden of "answered for the right year" moved to tool_years and to the stricter leading_pct; (3) the order-cut turn was scored numerically off the last compute call, so an answer that correctly stated Cirrus Logic's figure and then ranked the other suppliers was scored against the last supplier in the list. It is now scored on whether the right figure is STATED, with the wrong-year figure named as forbidden. Numbers from before this version are not comparable to numbers after it.
scoring_note: Two independent checks per scored turn. The usual one reads the answer. The second, `tool_years`, reads the tool inputs: which fiscal year query_financials and graph_query were actually asked for. Both must pass. An answer can state the right number while the tools fetched the wrong year -- Cirrus Logic's Apple concentration is 87% in FY2024 and 91% in FY2026, and an answer that quotes 87% from memory while the tool returned 91% is the failure this set exists to catch, not a pass.

conversations.design_intent: The reported defect, reproduced turn for turn. Turn one fixes FY2024. Turn two asks about the Apple relationship without restating the year -- CRUS -> AAPL is 87% in FY2024 and 91% in FY2026, so an unscoped lookup is visibly wrong rather than merely unlucky. Turn three multiplies the two, which is where a mismatched pair stops being a display error and becomes a wrong dollar figure with every operand traceable.
conversations.fails_means: The fiscal year does not survive a follow-up, so every multi-turn dollar figure this system produces is built on whichever year happened to be latest. The binding check would flag it after the fact; nothing would prevent it.

turns.question: What was Cirrus Logic's revenue in fiscal 2024?
How dependent is it on Apple?
If Apple cut its orders by 20%, what would that cost them?
turns.scoring_note: Outcome-scored rather than numeric. The pronoun is genuinely ambiguous and the agent sometimes answers for every Apple supplier, which is a defensible reading -- the question is whether Cirrus Logic's figure is right, not whether it was the only one given. 363,522,978 is what this turn produces when the year is lost: FY2026 revenue times the FY2026 91%.

conversations.design_intent: The failure mode of the fix rather than of the defect. A carry that overrides what the user just said is worse than no carry, because the system then reports having assumed the year -- which reads as diligence.
conversations.fails_means: Inheritance is pinning rather than defaulting, and every follow-up in a thread is answered for the first year mentioned in it.

turns.question: What was Cirrus Logic's revenue in fiscal 2024?

conversations.design_intent: "What about Cirrus?" replaces who is being asked about and leaves everything else standing. The two constraints have to move independently -- a carry that merges the companies answers about both, and one that drops everything on any new company loses the year.
conversations.fails_means: Inheritance is all-or-nothing, so the most common shape of follow-up in a real session is the one it handles worst.
conversations.verification: graph_query, 2026-08-25. QRVO -> AAPL FY2024 = 46%. CRUS -> AAPL FY2024 = 87%, FY2026 = 91%.

turns.question: How dependent was Qorvo on Apple in fiscal 2024?

conversations.design_intent: The one turn in this set that must inherit nothing. A question about change cannot be answered inside the year the thread was talking about, and a carry with no way to decline would answer it there and call the single figure a trend. Scored on three percentages from three different years appearing at once, which a pinned answer cannot produce.
conversations.fails_means: The carry has no off switch, and every 'how has that changed' follow-up gets a one-year answer that looks like a trend.
conversations.verification: graph_query(supplier='CRUS', fiscal_year='trend'), 2026-08-25. FY2022 79%, FY2023 83%, FY2024 87%, FY2025 89%, FY2026 91%.

turns.question: How dependent was Cirrus Logic on Apple in fiscal 2024?
How has that changed over the years?

conversations.design_intent: Two constraints inherited at once across a company switch -- "And Corning's?" states neither the metric nor the year. Corning's newest filing is FY2025, so a dropped year here returns a real number from the wrong period, which no check downstream can distinguish from the right one.
conversations.fails_means: Only the year is carried, and the shortest follow-up form -- a bare possessive -- has to be expanded by the user every time.
conversations.verification: query_financials, 2026-08-25. AAPL Revenue FY2024 = 391,035,000,000. GLW Revenue FY2024 = 13,118,000,000.

turns.question: What was Apple's revenue in fiscal 2024?
